classification.difficultyReason: Non-strict inequalities require distinguishing included equality boundaries from excluded poles.

answer.worked:
For $x\ne1$, $(x-1)^2>0$. Multiply by this square.
$$\begin{align*}x-1&\ge4(x-1)^2\\4(x-1)^2-(x-1)&\le0\\(x-1)(4x-5)&\le0\end{align*}$$
The polynomial inequality gives $1\le x\le\dfrac54$. Exclude $x=1$, so $1<x\le\dfrac54$.

For $x\ne-4$, $(x+4)^2>0$. Multiply by this square.
$$\begin{align*}3(x+4)&\le(x+4)^2\\(x+4)^2-3(x+4)&\ge0\\(x+4)(x+1)&\ge0\end{align*}$$
The polynomial inequality gives $x\le-4$ or $x\ge-1$. Exclude $x=-4$, so $x<-4$ or $x\ge-1$.

For $x\ne2$, $(x-2)^2>0$. Multiply by this square.
$$\begin{align*}x(x-2)&\ge-3(x-2)^2\\x(x-2)+3(x-2)^2&\ge0\\2(x-2)(2x-3)&\ge0\end{align*}$$
The polynomial inequality gives $x\le\dfrac32$ or $x\ge2$. Exclude $x=2$, so $x\le\dfrac32$ or $x>2$.

For $x\ne3$, $(x-3)^2>0$. Multiply by this square.
$$\begin{align*}(4x+1)(x-3)&\le2(x-3)^2\\(4x+1)(x-3)-2(x-3)^2&\le0\\(x-3)(2x+7)&\le0\end{align*}$$
The polynomial inequality gives $-\dfrac72\le x\le3$. Exclude $x=3$, so $-\dfrac72\le x<3$.

For $x\ne-2$, $(x+2)^2>0$. Multiply by this square.
$$\begin{align*}(x-3)(x+2)&\ge(x+2)^2\\(x-3)(x+2)-(x+2)^2&\ge0\\-5(x+2)&\ge0\end{align*}$$
This gives $x\le-2$. Exclude $x=-2$, so $x<-2$.

For $x\ne1$, $(x-1)^2>0$. Multiply by this square.
$$\begin{align*}(2x+5)(x-1)&\le-(x-1)^2\\(2x+5)(x-1)+(x-1)^2&\le0\\(x-1)(3x+4)&\le0\end{align*}$$
The polynomial inequality gives $-\dfrac43\le x\le1$. Exclude $x=1$, so $-\dfrac43\le x<1$.
